RESOLVER_TOOK_THREE_PASSES.lesson: Each pass returned a plausible number and each was wrong. The count moved 7 -> 8 -> 10 purely from resolver detail, with no change on disk. A census is only as good as its resolver, and a plausible count is not evidence the resolver is right.

NOT_RE_ATTESTED: No sidecar rewritten. Re-hashing certifies the present state and destroys the evidence that a repair broke an attestation.

FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.why_a_mismatch_is_EXPECTED: AS MEASURED 2026-08-18 12:52, these two are .PREREAD. sidecars and their mismatch is the cold-read workflow WORKING, not an attestation breaking. The project's practice is to hash the DRAFT bytes before a cold read so that subsequent patching is auditable. Verified on disk: PREREG_3d_replication_r179.PREREAD.sha256 written 2026-08-11 09:26:20 against a target of 09:29:36 (+3.3 min), and PREREG_3d_specificity_r178.PREREAD.sha256 written 09:17:20 against 09:22:50 (+5.5 min). A .PREREAD. digest that MATCHED the final file would mean the cold read changed nothing -- the mismatch is the mechanism reporting that it did.
FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.THE_DECLARATION_LIVES_ONLY_IN_THE_FILENA: Both sidecars were read in full at r348 and each contains EXACTLY ONE LINE -- a digest and a target name. Neither states that it is a pre-read snapshot or that divergence from the final file is expected. The only thing distinguishing an intentional draft snapshot from a broken attestation is the string '.PREREAD.' in the filename.
FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.WE_ARE_ON_THE_WRONG_SIDE_OF_OUR_OWN_RULE: A name is not a source. That rule has been confirmed five times in this corpus -- a scenario file named Grf15 carrying a 1.3 threshold, three stale headers, and FROZEN_MANIFEST nearly accepted on its name before summary.frozen_at was checked. These two sidecars are the same shape and we produced them.
FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.REMEDY_PROPOSED_NOT_APPLIED: One line inside each file stating what it is and that divergence from the final is expected. Not applied in this unit.
FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.SELF_DESCRIBING_AS_OF_r349: AS MEASURED 2026-08-18 13:12, both .PREREAD.sha256 files are SELF-DESCRIBING: each now carries a five-line '#' preamble stating that the digest is of the PRE-COLD-READ DRAFT, that the target named on the digest line is the FINAL file, and that a mismatch is EXPECTED and is the mechanism reporting that the cold read changed something. Before r349 the entire distinction between an intentional draft snapshot and a broken attestation lived in EIGHT CHARACTERS OF A FILENAME -- '.PREREAD.' -- and each file was 96 bytes holding one digest line and nothing else.
FALSE_BY_DESIGN_r348.MACHINE_VERIFIABILITY_TESTED_NOT_ASSUMED: Comment tolerance was tested empirically before writing: a scratch file with a leading '#' line verified 'OK' under sha256sum -c, exit 0. After the edit both sidecars still PARSE -- sha256sum reports '1 computed checksum did NOT match', which is the by-design draft-vs-final divergence, NOT a parse failure. The distinguishing check was run: 'no properly formatted checksum lines found' appears 0 times. Digests verified byte-identical to the pre-edit backups: b3379afc344a and eb7305921733.

FAILURE_MODE_TAXONOMY_r349.4_is_the_ONLY_ONE_CAUGHT_BY_READING: Modes 1-3 -- wrong scope, wrong resolver, unexamined taxonomy -- are invisible in the output and require RE-DERIVING THE METHOD to detect. The four modes therefore need two different defences, and neither substitutes for the other.
FAILURE_MODE_TAXONOMY_r349.4_rule: Before any markdown insertion in this corpus, locate the SENTENCE END -- '.**', a period followed by a blank line, or the closing emphasis marker -- never the line end. Appending to `sed -n 'Np'` output is appending mid-clause whenever the file is hard-wrapped.
